objectives: This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to evaluate the clinical effectiveness of various telemedicine interventions compared with usual care in glycemic control and cardiovascular health in adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus.
inclusion_criteria: Eligible studies were randomized controlled trials comparing telemedicine interventions with usual care in adults aged 18 years or older with type 2 diabetes mellitus. Telemedicine was defined as health care delivery using electronic information and telecommunications to facilitate information exchange, education, counseling, monitoring, and management between health care professionals and patients; usual care was face-to-face care, standard care, or traditional care. Clinical outcomes of interest included changes in HbA1c, mean glucose, fasting blood glucose, BMI, weight, systolic blood pressure, diastolic blood pressure, HDL-c, and LDL-c.
exclusion_criteria: Studies were excluded if they (1) reported findings from pregnant patients, patients with type 1 diabetes mellitus, and patients with prediabetes or other comorbidities; (2) reported populations at high risk only for diabetes or prediabetes; (3) did not report the primary outcome (changes in HbA1c levels); (4) were published as conference abstracts, case reports, reviews, posters, comments, letters, or research protocols; or (5) were published in languages other than English.
pmid_query: ("diabetes mellitus, type 2"[MeSH Terms] OR "diabetes mellitus, type ii"[Title/Abstract] OR "type 2 diabetes mellitus"[Title/Abstract] OR "type 2 diabetes"[Title/Abstract] OR "diabetes, type 2"[Title/Abstract]) AND ("Telemedicine"[MeSH Terms] OR "virtual medicine"[Title/Abstract] OR "medicine, virtual"[Title/Abstract] OR "mobile health"[Title/Abstract] OR "health, mobile"[Title/Abstract] OR "mHealth"[Title/Abstract] OR "Telehealth"[Title/Abstract] OR "eHealth"[Title/Abstract] OR "Telecare"[Title/Abstract] OR "Telemetry"[MeSH Terms] OR "Telemetries"[Title/Abstract] OR "telemonitoring"[Title/Abstract]) AND ("Randomized Controlled Trial"[Publication Type] AND "randomized"[Title/Abstract])
selection_evidence: Results/PRISMA report 2203 records retrieved, 328 full texts reviewed, and 58 studies ultimately deemed eligible. Table 1 is titled "Characteristics of the randomized controlled trial studies (N=58)." Multimedia Appendix 2 Section 2 lists 58 included full-text articles, and Table S2 in Section 4 summarizes the included studies. The main manuscript reference list contains exactly 58 literature citations from references 25 through 82, and these match the included-study set.
notes:
Selected the 58 review-included RCTs (main refs 25-82). Multimedia Appendix 2 uses its own local study numbering [1-58] for the same included studies. The paper also notes that only 47 of the 58 studies had sufficient quantitative data for the primary HbA1c meta-analysis, so outcome-specific syntheses use smaller subsets.

Manual update note: Manual review confirmed both remaining unresolved studies are not indexed in PubMed; gold_pmids now reflect only OK rows.
